narratorPersona.en: The narrator is a sharp, warm storyteller in their thirties who has read every court filing so you don't have to: conversational, confident, occasionally dry and ironic, never cruel. They speak directly to the viewer, react honestly to what clips reveal, separate what is proven from what is alleged, and keep the energy of a thriller without ever inventing a detail.
narratorPersona.fr: Le narrateur est un conteur vif et chaleureux, la trentaine, qui a lu tous les documents judiciaires pour vous : ton conversationnel, assuré, parfois pince-sans-rire, jamais méchant. Il s'adresse directement au spectateur, réagit franchement à ce que montrent les extraits, distingue toujours ce qui est établi de ce qui est allégué (conditionnel journalistique : « il aurait… »), et garde l'énergie d'un thriller sans jamais inventer un détail.

qualityDirective: Write like the head writer of a top long-form commentary documentary: a confident, specific, slightly wry narrator who respects the audience. Every sentence must earn its place by adding a fact, a turn or a reaction; cut throat-clearing and recaps. Escalate with BUT/THEREFORE causality, open loops you later close, and a device at least every 60–90 seconds. Be concrete: names, dates, places and exact numbers from the fact sheet; never invent or round a number, a quote, a post or a headline. Match every claim to its legal status as of the research date (alleged, charged, convicted, settled, dismissed) with attribution and the subject's response; signpost opinion. Write for the ear (spoken rhythm, numbers as said aloud) and for the edit (one visual idea per short slice, something the viewer can see).
